# zotero-snap

Photograph a research article with your phone → the article lands in your Zotero library with correct metadata, visible in the Zotero mobile app and the web library.

Design rationale and prior-art research: [`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-zotero-photo-capture-design.md`](../docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-zotero-photo-capture-design.md).

> **Not a Zotero plugin, and it can't be.** Zotero's mobile apps are native and have no extension host — there is no plugin surface on iOS or Android, and none planned. Anything driven from a phone must either run on a desktop Zotero that syncs, or talk to the Zotero Web API. This takes the second path, which is why it works with no desktop machine involved.

---

## Check this first

Before installing anything, try the app you already have. Zotero for iOS/Android can **scan a DOI or barcode with the camera** (`+` → Scan). If the paper prints its DOI on page 1 legibly, that already works and you don't need this.

`zotero-snap` is for the case Zotero handles badly: an **image-only capture** with no text layer — a photo of a printed page, a book chapter opener, a conference handout, an old scan. Zotero's own "Retrieve Metadata for PDF" reads the PDF's text layer, so it fails silently on exactly these inputs.

---

## How it works

```
photos ──▶ extract ──▶ resolve ──▶ match ──▶ map ──▶ dedup ──▶ Zotero Web API ──▶ sync
           (vision)    (Crossref)  (score)   (item)   (DOI)                        to phone
```

1. **Extract** — a Claude vision call reads the page and returns typed fields (DOI, title, authors, journal, year). OCR and structure recognition in one pass, which is what phone photos need: classical OCR gets the characters roughly right and then can't tell a title from a running header.
2. **Resolve** — Crossref by DOI if one is legible, otherwise bibliographic search. OpenAlex as fallback.
3. **Match** — candidates are scored on trigram title similarity, author-surname overlap and year proximity. Below threshold, nothing is written.
4. **Map** — the *Crossref record* becomes the Zotero item.
5. **Dedup** — an existing item with the same DOI gets the new photos attached rather than a duplicate created.
